sections.title: The Anointing at Bethany
observations: This passage highlights the significance of Mary anointing Jesus' feet with expensive perfume, symbolizing her devotion and the preparation for His burial.
The act of anointing is rich in biblical symbolism, often associated with kingship and the preparation for significant events.
Judas' objection reveals the tension between true worship and the misappropriation of resources for selfish gain.

sections.title: The Triumphal Entry
observations: Jesus' entry into Jerusalem on a donkey fulfills Old Testament prophecy, demonstrating His role as the humble King.
The crowd's response reflects a mix of genuine worship and misunderstanding of Jesus' mission, as they expected a political savior.
The use of palm branches signifies victory and celebration, but the true nature of Jesus' victory would be through His death and resurrection.

sections.title: Jesus Predicts His Death
observations: Jesus speaks of His impending death, emphasizing the necessity of His sacrifice for the salvation of many.
The metaphor of the grain of wheat illustrates the principle of dying to produce life, a central theme in the Gospel.
This section challenges readers to consider the cost of discipleship and the call to follow Jesus in His suffering.

sections.title: The Unbelief of the People
observations: Despite witnessing Jesus' miracles, many still did not believe, highlighting the theme of spiritual blindness.
Isaiah's prophecy is quoted to explain the unbelief, showing that God’s sovereignty is at work even in rejection.
This section serves as a sobering reminder of the hardness of human hearts and the need for divine intervention.

importantVerses.commentary: Mary's act of anointing Jesus with costly perfume signifies her deep love and devotion, foreshadowing His burial.
The crowd's proclamation of 'Hosanna' reflects their recognition of Jesus as the Messiah, though their understanding was limited.
Jesus' teaching about the grain of wheat illustrates the principle of sacrifice leading to greater life, central to His mission.
The contrast between Jesus' miracles and the people's unbelief underscores the theme of spiritual blindness.

questions: What does Mary's act of anointing Jesus teach us about true worship and devotion?
How does the crowd's response to Jesus' entry into Jerusalem reflect our own expectations of Him?
In what ways does Jesus' teaching about the grain of wheat challenge our understanding of sacrifice and discipleship?
What can we learn from the unbelief of the people despite witnessing Jesus' miracles?
